Refuse short comment openers in the disclosure D-4 reader (#283)

The disclosure case with '<!-->' in tools/test-build-site.py held only
for Python 3.14.4's reading of that opener. HTMLParser in Python 3.14.4
reads '<!-->' as 1 comment up to the next '-->' or '--!>', so the label
after it is not read as a tag. TODO 255 records that the case fails
under Python 3.14.7 in a side-by-side test.

Add SHORT_COMMENT, re.compile(r"<!---?>"), the same pattern as check 9
of tools/check-inline-code.py, and the exception ShortCommentRefused.
disclosure_d4_section() raises it, before it parses, on any text that
SHORT_COMMENT matches, so its result on these openers no longer comes
from the interpreter's HTMLParser; it still reads all other markup
with that parser. The refusal names the text found, '<!-->' or
'<!--->', without calling it a comment, as SHORT_COMMENT also matches
inside an attribute value. check_disclosure_states() catches only
ShortCommentRefused and reports it as a failure line, so any other
exception from the reader passes out instead of becoming a case
result. A new case pins that catch: it passes d4_failures() a stand-in
reader that raises, whose ShortCommentRefused must become the failure
line and whose ValueError must pass out unchanged. The '<!-->' case
now expects the refusal, and a new '<!--->' case expects it too. A new
'<!---->' case puts an Entry 5 label after the empty comment and the
note after the label, and expects the lacks-note failure, which it
gives only if the reader does not refuse the empty comment and reads
the label as a tag that ends D-4. The case does not show that the
reader parses '<!---->' as a comment, as a reading of it as text gives
the same result. The '<!-->' case is a fixture brought up to date with
a deliberate contract change: the test's reader now refuses the
openers that the generator's grammar and check 9 already refuse.

The comment on SHORT_COMMENT and the docstring of
disclosure_d4_section() also name the text '<!-->' or '<!--->'
wherever it stands. Check 9 of tools/check-inline-code.py searches a
page's whole text with the same pattern, so its message now names the
text found, as "the text '<!-->' in an HTML page", in place of "a
comment that opens as '<!-->'". Its docstring entry says that it
refuses that text wherever it stands, such as inside an attribute
value; what check 9 refuses is unchanged. A new case in
tools/test-inline-code.py puts '<!-->' in an attribute value and
requires that message, so it fails with the earlier one.

TODO 255 asks to make the case independent of the interpreter's
comment parsing, or to state the version the reading needs, with a
case that fails without the change. This change takes the first route.
The second, a version-conditional expected result, was declined. It
would key on sys.version_info < (3, 14, 7), a boundary not confirmed
in CPython, and it would fail on Python 3.14.4 under a simulated
short-close reading, where the '<!-->' case gives the lacks-note
failure. It would leave the case's result to the interpreter's comment
parsing, make the expected result depend on the version number too,
and give markup the generator refuses a meaning that changes by
release.

With only the refusal removed, the changed '<!-->' case and the new
'<!--->' case fail on Python 3.14.4 and under the simulated
short-close reading, and the new '<!---->' case passes under both.
With HTMLParser patched so that '<!---->' never closes, the '<!---->'
case is the only case of the disclosure group that fails. With it
patched so that it reads '<!---->' as text, no case of the group
fails. With the catch widened to except Exception, the stand-in reader
case is the only case of the group that fails.

Add .github/squash/283.txt, which holds this message byte for byte as
the message that the squash merge is to use.

The CPython change is not confirmed at source: the CPython source,
NEWS and changelog were not consulted, so the release that changed the
reading and the upstream issue remain unknown. TODO 255 does not
record how Python 3.14.7 reads '<!--->', and this message states no
Python 3.14.7 result other than the one TODO 255 records.
.python-version is untouched; moving the pin to 3.14.7 stays the
maintainer's decision.
